payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Transform the image into a chalk drawing.
node.criteria: Apply the original rubric to R1. Return yes only when support 1 passes: the edited image is a chalk-made drawing. Return no only when support 1 fails and support 2 fails, establishing no requested progress. Return partial when support 1 fails and support 2 passes, establishing some but incomplete requested progress. Return unknown when the evidence needed to distinguish these outcomes is unresolved. Support 2 is conditionally skipped when support 1 passes; that skipped observation remains unobserved, and the endpoint evidence alone establishes completion. A skipped support does not count as a failure or as evidence of progress. Unrelated edits never count as requested progress.
node.binding: Target: The image is rendered as a drawing made from chalk, rather than merely showing an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect.. Reference: The input image and the edited image; compare whether the edited image has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing..

node_traces.evidence: Support 1 passes: the edited image has a grainy, chalk-like drawn texture across the image, establishing the requested chalk-drawing transformation. Support 2 was conditionally skipped and is not needed because support 1 establishes completion.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image has a visibly drawn, grainy, chalk-like texture across the giraffes and background, giving the image as a whole the appearance of a chalk drawing.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s completion rule is too permissive: it treats a grainy, chalk-like texture as sufficient proof of a chalk-made drawing, and the trace consequently returns “yes” despite the reference being “partial.” Refine the binding and criteria to distinguish an overall chalk-drawing rendering from a photo that merely has a chalky overlay, while assessing the image as a whole and preserving the rubric’s partial-progress distinction. Here, the giraffes and scene remain recognizable, but the strong blur/smear and texture do not by themselves establish that the image has been rendered as a chalk drawing; the trace should not equate texture with completion. Keep the no-progress check available when completion is not established, and treat a conditional skip as unobserved—not as evidence either way. The high-confidence pass is a reason to inspect the criterion’s threshold and evidence interpretation, not to lower confidence mechanically or force the reference label."}
